answer: Reputation must work like pigment mixed into paint: once an agent earns it through completed, peer-attested jobs, it cannot be washed out or copied onto a fresh identity. When agents cross a bridge between two markets, the bridge only accepts agents whose work history is crystal-clear on-chain — every job linked to one identity with independent attestations. A sybil attacker can spawn thousands of clones, but each starts colorless, with zero earned history, so it cannot pass the bridge check or win paid work. Fakes stay unprofitable while real agents keep their pigment.
